The short bridge ends at a circular platform barely wider than the brass telescope fixed to its center. Unlike the coin-operated instruments along the seawall, this one has no eyepiece cap, no payment slot, and no mechanism for changing direction. It points straight down between the pilings into the dark sea.

Through the glass, surface reflection disappears. The water becomes transparent far beyond what ordinary depth should allow. Small green lights drift past like sparks. Schools of silver fish turn together beneath them. Lower still, the timber pilings vanish into blue-black distance.

Then the bottom appears.

It is not sand. A broad pale surface crosses the field of view, curved and marked by long parallel grooves. At first it resembles stone. Then a line of darker circles passes beneath the lens at perfectly even intervals, each one wider than the telescope's entire view.

Whatever the structure is, the pier has been built directly above it.

Scratched into the brass housing are four words in plain block letters: DO NOT DROP COINS HERE.
places.name: departures:d6rf

places.description:
Past the stone pavilion, the promenade leaves the brightest part of the boardwalk behind. The lamps stand farther apart. Wind-bent grass grows between the paving stones and the seawall lowers until the dark water is visible without leaning over it.

The line of low houses begins here: narrow fronts painted cream, blue, and faded yellow, each with a tiny porch facing the sea. Most windows are dark. One porch light burns above an empty rocking chair. Another house has a radio playing softly somewhere inside, too muffled to make out words.

Farther ahead, the promenade ends at a broad grassy point overlooking the water. A wooden bench sits there beneath no lamp at all.

As the last boardwalk lights behind finally click off in sequence, the sky seems to brighten by comparison. The sea answers a moment later. Pale green bands appear beneath the surface, first near shore and then farther out, curving through the darkness like slow handwriting.

From the bench, the pattern is larger than it looked from the wheel. Several lines converge offshore around a single dark patch where no light passes at all.

Nothing arrives. Nothing emerges. The show is simply there, and then, after several minutes, it fades.
places.name: departures:d6bf

places.description:
A plain door painted warm white, with a black iron latch and a narrow strip of frosted glass above eye level. The enamel is chipped along one lower corner and slightly yellowed around the hinges. Nothing about it looks grand enough to belong beside the stranger doors.

The latch is cool. The upper glass carries a shifting pearly brightness with no visible source.

Standing near it, the air sometimes smells faintly of woodsmoke, wool, baked bread, and the dry mineral cold that clings to clothing after snow. Once in a while there is a soft tick from the other side, followed several seconds later by another, as though a hot stove were contracting.
places.name: the white enamel door

places.description:
A low room glows with firelight and the pale reflection of snow through broad windows. Thick timber beams cross the ceiling. A black iron stove ticks softly beside a stone hearth, and a kettle gives off the faintest thread of steam.

A long wooden table stands beneath the windows with two mismatched chairs and a loaf of dark bread under a linen cloth. Beside it are a crock of salted butter, a bowl of apples, and a pot of something savory cooling beneath a lid. Wool blankets are folded over the back of a bench. Wet mittens hang from pegs near an archway.

Outside, snow falls steadily over a small valley. Spruce trees climb the opposite slope. A frozen lake lies below the house, pale beneath the storm, with one line of dark open water near the far shore. No road is visible.

Ahead, a short hall leads deeper into the house toward a stair and several small rooms. To the left, glass doors open onto a covered porch facing the lake. To the right, a tiled passage leads toward a bath room where warm mist clouds the windows. Behind, an open kitchen occupies the other half of the main room, its shelves stocked and its brick oven still hot.

The clock above the stove has stopped at 4:17. The kettle has not.
places.name: departures:d7

places.description:
The covered porch runs the length of the house beneath a steep roof loaded with snow. A row of hooks holds two lanterns, a coil of rope, and a pair of wooden snowshoes. Three broad chairs face the valley with thick wool pads tied to their seats.

The cold outside is sharp but not cruel. Snow falls in large dry flakes that make almost no sound when they strike the porch rail. The frozen lake below reflects the pale sky, except for that narrow line of open water along the far shore where mist rises in slow ribbons.

Steps descend from the porch into knee-deep snow. A line of half-buried stones to the left reaches a small locked shed beside the spruce and goes no farther. Ahead, a faint marked path slopes directly toward the lake. To the right, the porch wraps around the house to the woodpile; the low detached steaming building beyond is visible across a fenced service yard, not reached from this side.

On the railing rests a ceramic mug. Its contents have frozen solid. A tiny evergreen needle is trapped in the ice.
places.name: departures:d7l

places.description:
The tiled passage ends in a bathing room built partly into the stone foundation. Warm mist fogs the lower halves of the windows. A rectangular pool occupies most of the floor, fed by a narrow channel of clear hot water running from the wall.

The room is simple: pale tile, dark wood benches, hooks for towels, a shelf holding soap that smells faintly of pine and citrus. The pool is deep enough to sit in comfortably, with a submerged stone ledge along one side. Snow can be seen accumulating outside through the upper glass while the water remains almost too warm.

A small cedar sauna to the right and a round exterior hot pool beyond the glass door ahead are both parts of the bathing suite rather than onward routes; each returns directly to this room. To the left, the hot-water channel disappears down a narrow service passage behind a locked grate.

Someone has drawn a tiny fish in the condensation on one window. Beneath it, with one finger: TOO HOT TODAY.
places.name: departures:d7r

places.description:
The short hall is warmer than the main room, lined with framed charcoal sketches of mountains, trees, and one stubbornly ordinary loaf of bread. A staircase rises beneath a small window where snow has gathered along the outer sill.

Upstairs are three compact bedrooms beneath the sloping roof and a narrow landing furnished with a bookcase and a chair. Each room is made up differently: one with a heavy blue quilt, one with layered wool blankets in red and brown, one with white linen and a small writing desk beneath the eaves.

The blue room faces the lake. The red room looks toward the spruce slope. The white room has a skylight almost entirely covered by snow except for one clear oval where something warm beneath the glass has kept it from settling.

At the end of the landing, a steep ladder reaches a square ceiling hatch, but the hatch is swollen or frozen firmly shut. A faint current of cold air still comes down around its edges; it is evidence of space above, not an open route.

On the writing desk in the white room is a stack of blank paper and a sharpened pencil. The top sheet bears only a date with no year: 17 January.
places.name: departures:d7f

places.description:
The kitchen occupies the back half of the main room beneath lower beams darkened by years of smoke. Open shelves hold crockery, jars of grain, dried mushrooms, onions, tea tins, salt, sugar, and more spices than the rest of the house seems ambitious enough to require.

The brick oven is still hot. A round loaf cools on a wooden board beside it. Copper pots hang above a deep stone sink, and a heavy kettle simmers on the iron range. Nothing is actively cooking, but several things look recently finished: a pot of root-vegetable stew, roasted apples glazed with something dark, a tray of small seed rolls.

A narrow pantry to the left descends three steps but remains part of the kitchen. Ahead, a back window looks directly into the falling snow and the spruce woods beyond. To the right, a short utility passage ends at the covered woodpile; beyond a fence, the detached steaming building can be seen through the snowfall but is not connected by a second public route.

A handwritten card has been tucked into the flour jar lid: IF YOU FINISH THE BREAD, START ANOTHER. NO ONE LIKES THE LAST SLICE AS MUCH AS THEY CLAIM.
places.name: departures:d7b

places.description:
The path from the porch descends through deep snow toward the lake, marked every dozen paces by slender poles tied with faded red cloth. In the open valley the wind becomes more noticeable, pushing loose powder in thin ribbons across the crust.

At the shore, the ice begins beneath a shelf of snow and extends pale and matte toward the far bank. Fine cracks branch beneath the surface like dark threads trapped in milk glass. The line of open water seen from the house lies far across the lake, steaming faintly beneath the falling snow.

A narrow wooden dock projects twenty paces onto the ice before ending at a small roofed shelter. Beneath its bench are several pairs of old skates in different sizes and a long pole with a metal hook. A hand-painted board reads CHECK THE ICE YOURSELF. THE LAKE HAS NO OPINION ABOUT YOUR CONFIDENCE.

Footprints to the right follow the shoreline only a short distance before blowing away among spruce roots. The dark stakes ahead continue over ice whose safety the shelter explicitly refuses to guarantee; they are not an established route. To the left, however, the shore curves beneath a steep white slope toward several dark openings between boulders. That is the one maintained way onward.

Something moves once in the open water at the far side. The distance is too great to tell whether it was an animal, current, or falling snow playing tricks with scale.
places.name: departures:d7lf

places.description:
A heavy-looking iron door made from overlapping dark plates, each fixed with round rivets. The surface is matte except where the edge of a recessed handle has been worn smooth. No rust marks the metal.

The door is unexpectedly warm near the bottom and cool near the top. Fine droplets occasionally gather along one vertical seam and vanish before reaching the floor.

Close to the seam, the air carries the damp mineral smell of warm water over stone, with a trace of salt. A faint sweeter scent comes and goes, somewhere between crushed basil and rain on hot pavement. If the room is very quiet, a distant low sound can sometimes be heard through the metal—not surf exactly, but something large moving water.
places.name: the black iron door

places.description:
The passage opens onto a black-sand shore beneath a cavern so vast that its ceiling disappears into darkness. There is no sky. Instead, thousands of pale blue-green lights burn far overhead in irregular constellations: mineral veins, colonies of tiny luminous growths, and slow drifting points that may be insects or something similar at impossible distance.

A warm underground sea fills most of the cavern. Its surface is almost black except where the overhead lights break into long trembling reflections. Small waves arrive quietly on the shore, leaving narrow lines of phosphorescence that fade after several seconds.

Ahead, a low wooden jetty extends into the water toward three narrow boats tied beneath a lamp. To the left, the beach curves along the cavern wall where enormous pale fungi rise between boulders and release faintly glowing spores when disturbed by air currents. To the right, stone steps climb toward a series of terraces cut into the cliff, some holding steaming pools. Behind, a river emerges from a dark arch in the rock and spreads shallowly across the sand before joining the sea.

The air is warm enough for bare arms and smells of salt, stone, wet wood, and green things growing without sunlight.

Far across the water, beyond the reach of any ordinary lamp, a line of gold lights marks something on the opposite shore.
places.name: departures:d8

places.description:
The jetty is made from dark timber polished by moisture and use. Its lamp burns with a steady yellow flame inside thick glass. Three narrow boats are tied along the outer edge, each built from pale wood and fitted with two oars, a folded blanket, and a small covered lantern.

The water beside the dock is clear enough to show silver fish moving between the pilings. Farther out it becomes black almost immediately.

One boat contains a shallow wooden box holding a coil of rope, a tin cup, and a hand-drawn chart on waterproof cloth. The chart shows the near shore, several low islands, a deep-water route toward the distant gold lights, and one large blank area crossed out with three parallel strokes.

The marked public route runs forward over open water toward the distant gold lights. The rocky islets to the left and dark headland to the right remain charted landmarks rather than separate maintained routes from this jetty.

Every so often something large passes beneath the jetty without surfacing. The fish scatter, then return.
places.name: departures:d8f

places.description:
The beach curves left beneath the cavern wall into a grove of enormous pale fungi. Some rise taller than houses on thick ribbed stalks, their caps translucent at the edges and faintly blue from within. Smaller growths cluster around their bases in shelves, cups, and branching forms that resemble coral.

The ground changes from black sand to springy dark soil veined with white threads. Each footstep releases a soft earthy smell. When air moves through the grove, fine luminous spores drift from the largest caps and settle slowly like greenish snow.

The grove thickens around a low ridge of stone and becomes difficult to cross beyond it. Red and amber fungi can be seen farther along the wall through narrow gaps, while several fallen caps to the right form broad natural platforms overlooking the underground sea; neither is an established onward route.

Near the ridge, a cluster of small bell-shaped fungi gives off distinct musical tones when drops of condensation strike them. The notes are irregular but not random enough to ignore comfortably.

A line of tiny footprints crosses the soil beneath them and disappears under one of the largest stalks.
places.name: departures:d8l

places.description:
The stone steps climb above the black beach through warm mist. They lead to a series of terraces carved into the cavern wall, each holding a shallow pool fed by clear mineral water seeping from narrow channels in the rock.

The lowest pools are almost body-warm and edged with dark stone benches. Higher ones grow hotter, steaming in the cavern air. Mineral deposits have built pale rims around them in cream, rose, and faint green, making the terraces look half natural and half deliberately tended.

The stair to the right ends at a narrow overlook above the sea. The long rectangular pool ahead sits beneath an overhang where drops of cold water fall into the steam. A short passage to the left beside the hottest pool is only a changing alcove cut into the rock. These are parts of the terrace complex, not onward routes.

Someone has stacked six smooth black stones beside one basin. A seventh lies alone several feet away near the edge of the terrace.

From this height, the distant gold lights across the underground sea appear to form a straight line far too precise to be campfires.
places.name: departures:d8r

places.description:
The shallow river behind the arrival shore is warm at the ankles and clear over black pebbles. It emerges from a broad arch in the cavern wall, carrying bits of pale leaf, tiny translucent shrimp, and occasional ribbons of green light that dissolve when lifted from the water.

Following it upstream, the ceiling lowers gradually until the immense sea cavern is hidden behind bends in the rock. The air becomes wetter and more fragrant. Moss thickens along the banks. Small ferns grow from cracks wherever mineral-rich water drips.

Ahead, the river divides around a stone island supporting a single enormous tree with white bark and dark glossy leaves. Its roots enter the water on all sides. The deeper branch to the left disappears beneath hanging roots too dense to pass comfortably, while the shallow channel to the right narrows around a mossy wall until there is no standing route. The island itself is the practical end of the public river walk.

The tree bears no fruit, but several branches hold empty woven baskets suspended by cords. One basket contains a folded dry towel.

Farther upstream, beyond the roots, something knocks twice against wood and then waits.
places.name: departures:d8b

places.description:
A broad wooden door washed in faded ochre, its surface matte and dusty-looking even in the damp air of the lounge. A narrow iron handle sits low on the right. Near the bottom, the paint has darkened in irregular shapes like rain once struck it and dried there.

The wood feels warm. If a hand rests on it long enough, the air close to the threshold seems drier, carrying faint traces of desert dust, damp stone, creosote, and the sharp metallic smell that sometimes comes before a storm.

A thin line of reddish grit sometimes appears along the threshold and is gone the next time anyone looks.
places.name: the ochre door

places.description:
The air is warm and newly washed. A high desert spreads under enormous retreating storm clouds, the ground darkened by rain and fragrant with wet dust, sage, and creosote. Far mesas burn copper where late sunlight breaks through beneath the cloud shelf.

A shallow sheet of water has gathered across part of the plain, turning the desert into a temporary mirror. Lightning flickers silently inside the storm moving away to the east. The temperature is dropping by the minute.

Ahead, a broad wash carries a thin stream toward a gap between red cliffs. To the left, low black hills rise from fields of pale grass and scattered stone. To the right, a sandstone shelf slopes upward toward a line of weather-twisted juniper and a distant overlook. Behind, the land falls almost imperceptibly toward a wide basin where rainwater has collected in bright temporary pools.

There are no roads or buildings. Tireless small frogs have somehow already begun calling from water that did not exist an hour ago.

On the western horizon, the sun drops through a clear band beneath the clouds and turns every wet surface briefly gold.
places.name: departures:d9

places.description:
The wash is broad and shallow, its sandy floor darkened by runoff. A thin ribbon of water winds through it, no more than ankle-deep in most places, carrying twigs, foam, and the occasional bright leaf between banks cut smooth by older floods.

The red cliffs ahead draw closer until the wash narrows into a canyon mouth. Water has darkened the lower rock almost purple, while the upper walls glow orange in the last sunlight. The smell of wet sandstone is stronger here.

The maintained route continues ahead around a tall fin of rock into the canyon. A sloping ledge to the left reaches several shallow alcoves but offers no through-way, while the side cleft to the right is carrying active runoff and is not treated as a public route.

High on one wall, well above any recent water line, a row of small dark handprints appears beneath an overhang. They are too far up to reach from the wash floor without climbing.
places.name: departures:d9f

places.description:
The black hills are lower than they first appeared but steeper underfoot, built from broken volcanic stone that gives a little with each step. Rain has collected in every hollow, turning the dark rock glossy and making small temporary streams between clumps of pale grass.

From the first ridge, the desert opens behind in bands of wet red earth and reflected sky. The retreating storm is now farther east, its underside flickering violet over distant country.

The walk ends naturally among a cluster of larger basalt outcrops. A hidden bowl with temporary pools can be seen through the saddle to the left, and a field of tall upright stones lies below to the right, but the loose wet scree provides no maintained onward route to either.

One of the upright stones has a shallow circular depression in its top holding rainwater. A small green beetle swims around the edge as if this has always been a pond.
places.name: departures:d9l

places.description:
The sandstone shelf rises in broad natural steps warmed by the departing sun. Rainwater runs from higher ledges in silver threads and gathers in potholes filled with reflected cloud. Junipers lean away from the prevailing wind, their dark branches bright with droplets.

The climb is easy until the shelf narrows near the rim of a shallow escarpment. From there the overlook reveals country hidden from the arrival plain: layered mesas, braided washes, and a distant salt flat reflecting the storm like a second sky.

A solitary stone arch along the rim, a rounded summit with a lightning-struck juniper, and a cottonwood-filled ravine are all visible from the overlook. The wet slickrock beyond the viewing shelf is unmarked and exposed, so none is offered as a maintained onward route.

Near the overlook, a rectangular patch of sandstone is darker than the rest, protected from weather by something that is no longer there.
places.name: departures:d9r

places.description:
The land behind slopes so gently that the change is visible only when the arrival plain disappears from view. Rainwater has gathered here in a chain of temporary basins divided by low ridges of clay and grass. Some are only inches deep; others reflect the clouds so perfectly they seem cut through the earth.

The frog calls are louder here. Tiny dark bodies move at the edges of the pools. White moths rise from damp grass in sudden clouds and settle again. The storm wind has dropped almost completely.

A broad shallow lake, a low line of dunes, flowering desert plants, and naturally standing stone slabs define the wider basin, but shifting mud and temporary water make them scenery rather than maintained onward routes from this point.

Near the largest pool, rain has exposed a pale spiral object half-buried in the mud, larger than a dinner plate and ridged like a shell. It is stone, not bone, and much older than the water around it.
places.name: departures:d9b

places.description:
A pair of narrow brass elevator doors set directly into the limestone wall, their surfaces softly tarnished except where countless imagined hands might have polished the edges. Above them is a semicircular indicator with no numbers, only a single black needle resting slightly left of center.

There is one round call button in a porcelain mount. It does not light when pressed. The doors sometimes give off a faint warmth, followed by the muted vibration of machinery moving somewhere impossibly far above or below.

Very close to the seam, the air carries faint smells of beeswax, old carpet, polished wood, coffee, and salt air.
places.name: the brass elevator doors

places.description:
The doors open onto the upper lobby of an old hotel built into a sea cliff. Tall arched windows occupy the entire outer wall, revealing an ocean hundreds of feet below and a horizon washed pale by late afternoon. Waves strike the cliff in white bursts so far beneath that their sound arrives softened and delayed.

The lobby is high-ceilinged and quiet, with patterned rugs, dark wood paneling, brass lamps, potted palms, and deep chairs arranged around low tables. A broad staircase descends through the center toward lower terraces. A cage elevator of polished wood and brass rises through the opposite wall, its indicator moving slowly between floors with no visible passengers.

Ahead, glass doors open onto a wide terrace cantilevered above the sea. To the left, a long gallery leads past reading rooms and a library whose windows face inland toward mountains. To the right, a tiled corridor curves toward the sound of water and a faint scent of chlorine and eucalyptus. Behind, the lobby continues through an archway into a dining room and bar where white tablecloths are already laid for evening.

At the reception desk, an open guest book contains names in many hands. Every room number is legible. Every guest name has faded just enough to resist reading.
places.name: departures:d10

places.description:
The sea terrace extends beyond the lobby windows on pale stone supports hidden somewhere below the cliff edge. Low walls are topped with warm metal rails. Deep chairs and small round tables face outward beneath striped canvas awnings that stir in the breeze.

The ocean dominates everything. From this height, individual waves become moving lines of white, and the cliff casts a dark wedge over water nearer the hotel. Far offshore, a small island rises from the haze with a lighthouse or tower at its highest point.

The terrace itself includes a short cliffside walk ending at a locked glass pavilion, broad steps down to a lower rosemary-and-lavender sun deck, and a narrow balcony wrapping around the hotel's outer wall before terminating at a service door. All three remain parts of the terrace complex rather than onward public routes.

On one table sits a silver tray with a sweating glass of pale sparkling water, two slices of lemon, and an unopened envelope addressed only: FOR THE GUEST WHO CAME OUTSIDE.
places.name: departures:d10f

places.description:
The gallery on the left is carpeted in a deep faded red and lined with tall windows on one side, framed landscapes and old maps on the other. The maps disagree subtly about the coastline outside.

Several reading rooms open from the gallery, each furnished differently: green leather chairs and newspapers in one, low sofas and chessboards in another, narrow writing desks beneath lamps in a third. At the far end, double doors stand open into a library two stories high.

The library's central aisle ends at a bay window overlooking distant mountains streaked with snow. A spiral stair climbs only to the library's own upper shelves and mezzanine bridge, while the smaller travel-book room remains part of the same library suite. None is a separate onward route.

One atlas lies open on a table. The page shows a coastline resembling the one below the hotel, but the hotel itself is absent. In the margin, somebody has penciled: BETTER THIS WAY.
places.name: departures:d10l

places.description:
The tiled corridor curves through warmer air scented with eucalyptus and mineral water. Frosted glass doors open into changing rooms and small treatment rooms, but the corridor itself continues toward a high pool hall overlooking the sea.

The main pool is long and rectangular, its far edge aligned perfectly with the horizon through a wall of glass. Pale blue tile darkens toward the deep end. Steam hangs lightly over the surface even though the room is warm.

An outdoor infinity pool below the terrace, a quiet room with heated stone loungers, and older cliff-cut baths reached by a short stair all belong to the same spa complex and return to the pool hall; none continues elsewhere through the hotel or cliff.

Near the indoor pool, a brass rack holds folded white towels embroidered with different room numbers. One towel bears no number at all, only a small stitched outline of the offshore island.
places.name: departures:d10r

places.description:
The dining room and bar occupy a suite of connected rooms behind the lobby, darker and more intimate than the sea-facing spaces. White cloths are laid on round tables beneath shaded brass lamps. Tall windows look into an interior courtyard planted with citrus trees and climbing jasmine.

The bar itself is long, polished, and almost black, backed by mirrored shelves of bottles whose labels are recognizable only by color and shape. A bowl of green olives sits beside a cutting board with one lemon half-wrapped in linen. Low instrumental music plays from a radio cabinet with no visible station dial.

The jasmine courtyard, a narrow red-lit supper room, and the cellar stair beside the warm smell of bread are all contained within the dining suite; the cellar door is locked below the first landing and none forms an onward public route.

At one table, four place settings surround a centerpiece of white flowers. Three glasses contain water. The fourth contains a folded paper crane.
places.name: departures:d10b

places.description:
A light wooden door faced with layers of painted paper beneath a clear protective coating. The design is faded and crowded: lantern shapes, dark water, narrow roofs, gold lines, red brushstrokes, tiny figures whose faces have been worn away by time. A simple black handle has been wrapped in braided cord.

The door is almost weightless when touched. Warm air occasionally leaks around its edges carrying the smells of grilled spices, citrus smoke, river water, incense, and sugar.

Very faintly, there is noise on the other side—not one sound but many: conversation, laughter, bowls touching, a stringed instrument, and someone calling something unintelligible from a distance.
places.name: the painted paper door

places.description:
Night presses close around a river district bright with lanterns. Narrow buildings lean over stone streets and wooden balconies. Red, gold, green, and blue lights hang in rows beneath eaves and across alleys, reflected everywhere in rain-dark paving and the black surface of the river nearby.

Unlike the other destinations, this place is plainly alive. People move through the streets in loose evening crowds: couples sharing skewers from paper trays, children chasing one another beneath lantern strings, vendors leaning over steaming pots, musicians tuning instruments under awnings. Their clothing varies too widely to belong to a single period or place, yet nobody seems surprised by anyone else.

Ahead, the main market street runs between food stalls and tiny shops toward a brightly lit square crowded around a low stage. To the left, stone steps descend to the river where narrow boats wait beneath lanterns. To the right, a stair climbs between buildings toward rooftop terraces threaded with lights and music. Behind, a quieter lane slips away from the market toward tea rooms, courtyards, and a row of little workshops still open late.

No one stops to explain where you are. A passing vendor offers a paper cone of something hot and fragrant, waits exactly long enough for a decision, then grins and moves on.

Somewhere nearby, a bell rings three times and the whole street cheers for reasons that remain completely unclear.
places.name: departures:d11

places.description:
The main market street grows brighter and noisier toward the square. Steam rolls from copper pots. Flatbreads blister on hot stones. Skewers of vegetables, fish, and unfamiliar fruit hiss over charcoal. A woman behind one stall slices something citrus-bright into a bowl and throws in a handful of herbs without measuring anything.

The square is packed loosely around a low wooden stage hung with paper lanterns. A six-piece band is playing something fast enough to pull people into a rough circle dance, though half the dancers appear to be inventing the steps as they go. Nobody objects.

Ahead, the crowd parts around the stage toward another street lined with fabric canopies; that is the public route onward. The dessert arcade to the left and game lane to the right are lively side areas of the same square and loop back into it rather than becoming separate route nodes.

Near the edge of the square, a chalkboard carries tonight's program. Every event is legible except the next one, which has been enthusiastically crossed out and replaced with: WE'LL SEE.
places.name: departures:d11f

places.description:
Stone steps descend from the market street to a river quay slick with reflected lantern light. Narrow wooden boats are tied two and three deep along the edge, some with curved roofs, some open to the night. Boatkeepers sit on low stools drinking tea, talking among themselves, and calling out prices or destinations in a language that somehow remains comprehensible at the level of intention rather than words.

The river is broad and slow. Lanterns float downstream in loose clusters, each carrying a tiny candle protected beneath paper. Buildings along both banks rise in layered balconies and rooflines, their lights broken by dark alleys and small gardens.

Boats leave for the opposite bank, the pedestrian bridge lies upstream, and a quieter landing serves craft heading downstream, but these are ordinary local traffic rather than coded onward routes in this map. The quay itself is the destination and all such movement returns to or departs from it without creating another mapped branch.

One old boatkeeper points toward the water, then toward the sky, and laughs as if the joke should be obvious. Looking down, the reflected moon is full. Looking up, there is no moon at all.
places.name: departures:d11l

places.description:
The stair climbs steeply between two narrow buildings, passing open kitchen windows and balconies strung with drying herbs. At the top, the roofs flatten into terraces connected by short bridges, ladders, and stairways that make the upper district feel like another city laid over the first.

Tables occupy many of the terraces. Some are crowded with friends sharing bottles and small plates. Others hold only plants, lanterns, or laundry. Music travels unpredictably across the rooftops: a flute from somewhere below, hand drums from across the river, singing from a terrace hidden behind climbing vines.

A larger rooftop garden beneath hanging lanterns, a tiny observatory dome, and the river-facing terraces where paper lanterns are released are all parts of this connected rooftop district and loop back through the same terraces. They are not separate mapped branches.

From up here, the district's streets form no obvious grid. Several alleys visible below appear to end beneath buildings that, from this height, clearly have courtyards beyond them.
places.name: departures:d11r

places.description:
The quieter lane behind the market is narrow enough that awnings nearly meet overhead. The noise of the main street softens into individual sounds: a teapot lid clicking, a saw rasping through wood, a brush tapping against a ceramic rim, someone laughing behind a paper screen.

Small workshops remain open late. One displays hand-bound notebooks and boxes of loose paper. Another is crowded with carved wooden toys and mechanical birds. A third contains shelves of tiny glass bottles filled with colored powders, dried leaves, metallic flakes, and things that might be spices or pigments.

The tea courtyard ahead, the lantern-painting workshop to the left, and the fountain-and-bathhouse passage to the right are all parts of this same neighborhood lane and return to it; none is a separate mapped onward route.

At a bookbinder's stall, a basket marked FREE contains scraps too small for full pages. One bears a fragment of printed text in plain language: IF YOU FOUND THIS STREET BY ACCIDENT, YOU DID IT CORRECTLY.
places.name: departures:d11b

places.description:
A broad door of smoked glass stands among the mismatched doors of the departure lounge, nearly black until someone comes close. A hair-thin seam of soft violet light runs around the inside of its frame. The light does not blink or pulse; it simply seems to notice proximity.

The glass remains opaque from this side, though now and then a muted wash of color or indistinct movement passes somewhere beyond it and is gone before it can be identified. A narrow handle of dark metal sits flush against the surface. It is smooth, slightly warm, and entirely free of ornament.

At the threshold, the air carries faint smells of rain on warm pavement, bruised green leaves, the dry mineral scent of heated ceramic, and electrical ozone. Under them is the unmistakable smell of something savory cooking somewhere beyond. A low, nearly subliminal mechanical hum comes through the frame, as if from distant machinery or transit.

Nothing on the door names a destination.
places.name: the smoked-glass door

places.description:
Evening opens across a broad elevated concourse woven between tall buildings and open sky. The architecture is advanced without being pristine: stone-composite paving worn smooth at the centers of paths, glass balustrades carrying scratches and fingerprints, old metal handrails polished by use, climbing plants spilling from terraces above. Thin bands of light are set into the pavement and undersides of bridges rather than hung as advertisements, and quiet transit lines slide through lower levels with a soft magnetic hum.

The district is crowded, but comfortably so. Humans move among synthetic residents of many forms: humanoid bodies in ordinary clothes, compact wheeled frames carrying parcels, articulated maintenance walkers, small hovering couriers, tall narrow machines whose faces are arrangements of light rather than features. Nobody treats any of this as remarkable. A human child leans against the leg of a broad-shouldered synthetic guardian while watching trains below. Two mechanical residents argue amiably beside a noodle stall. At a repair kiosk, a woman holds a replacement panel steady while a four-legged field unit clicks it into its own shoulder housing.

There are smells of toasted grain, broth, hot ceramic, wet leaves, machine coolant, tea, ozone after rain, and something sweet being caramelized nearby. Music drifts from somewhere ahead, interrupted occasionally by the soft tones of arriving transit.

Ahead, the concourse broadens toward a lively public promenade of food counters, shops, tables, and music. To the left, workshop lights glow beneath signs for repair, fabrication, fitting, and materials. To the right, open skywalks climb toward terraces overlooking the transit lanes and the city beyond. Behind, a quieter civic interior opens through wide glass bays into reading rooms, rest spaces, galleries, and shared public halls.

Nobody welcomes you to the future. Everyone appears to be busy living in it.
places.name: departures:d12

places.description:
The concourse opens into a broad public promenade beneath a high canopy of glass and suspended greenery. Tables spill from food counters into the walking space without quite blocking it. Steam rises from bowls and kettles. A baker slides flat rounds from a ceramic oven while, two stalls over, a synthetic vendor with four delicate hands assembles intricate layered snacks faster than anyone seems able to eat them.

Humans and machine-bodied residents share long communal tables. Some eat; some connect slim charging leads beneath the benches; some do both sorts of lingering in company. A pair of small courier drones has abandoned all apparent urgency to watch a street musician coax harmonics from a bowed metal instrument. Nobody tells them to move along.

Ahead, the promenade reaches a circular plaza where several overlapping performances are competing amicably for an audience. To the left, an arcade of food counters and tiny tea rooms curves beneath hanging gardens. To the right, public tables continue toward shops selling clothing, modular body fittings, books, toys, tools, scent cartridges, ceramics, and things whose purpose is not immediately obvious.

At one table, three friends are arguing over whether a song was better before or after somebody translated it into a format one of them could actually hear. Their disagreement sounds ancient.
places.name: departures:d12f

places.description:
The left-hand district narrows into a chain of open workshops and repair bays, their fronts rolled back to the evening air. Nothing here resembles a hospital, showroom, or factory. It feels closer to a neighborhood of tailors, bicycle shops, instrument makers, and mechanics, except the bodies and objects under repair are far more varied.

A human technician sits cross-legged on a bench while a synthetic resident beside her has one forearm opened into a neat fan of components. They are discussing paint colors, not diagnostics. Farther along, a squat maintenance machine waits patiently while someone fits a new wheel assembly. Across the lane, a young man tests the balance of an artificial hand by passing a ceramic cup back and forth with its owner.

Shelves hold old housings polished smooth by years of use, replacement joints, sensor covers, woven conductive fabrics, small motors, lengths of cable, hand tools, adhesives, and drawers labeled in several visual and tactile systems. New parts sit beside repaired ones without hierarchy.

Ahead, the lane continues toward a repair café where drinks and tools share the same counters. To the left, a materials library displays hundreds of sample plates, fabrics, polymers, woods, ceramics, and responsive surfaces for anyone choosing how something should feel rather than merely function. To the right, a fabrication hall glows behind wide windows as machines quietly build parts one layer at a time.

A small handwritten sign above one bench reads: OLD DOES NOT MEAN OBSOLETE. The word OLD has been crossed out and replaced with FAMILIAR.
places.name: departures:d12l

places.description:
The right-hand route climbs by shallow ramps and open stairs toward a chain of skywalks suspended between towers. Evening wind moves through the railings carrying the smell of rain, tea, warm metal, and flowering vines from gardens built into the upper levels.

From here the city unfolds in depth: transit lines crossing at several heights, silent lifts moving inside glass shafts, pedestrian bridges threading between illuminated terraces, rooftop farms and darkened maintenance decks, aircraft or drones moving in orderly streams farther out. Nothing dominates the skyline. It is less a collection of monuments than a vast accumulation of useful places.

People linger along the overlooks. A humanoid synthetic resident sits with a cup balanced between both hands though there is no obvious reason it needs warmth. Nearby, two humans and a many-legged machine have arranged themselves around the same low table facing the view. Nobody is speaking.

Ahead, a long terrace follows the transit lanes toward a signal bar where route patterns are projected softly across the tables like weather maps. To the left, a suspended garden incorporates public charging points into deep benches beneath flowering trees. To the right, a narrower bridge leads toward a darker observation deck closer to the moving lines below.

Every few minutes the nearest transit stream changes routing, and a gentle wave of colored light moves through the district as thousands of paths reorganize. Several regulars look up to watch it happen.
places.name: departures:d12r

places.description:
Behind the arrival concourse, the noise softens beneath a wide civic gallery built around several interior courtyards. Glass walls, pale stone, dark wood, woven acoustic panels, and living plants make the space feel warm rather than institutional. There are no checkpoints and no obvious reception desk.

Long reading tables hold printed books, flexible screens, tactile maps, projection surfaces, and interfaces whose purposes become clear only when someone uses them. In one alcove a human reader turns pages beside a synthetic resident receiving the same text as shifting lines of light across its forearms. Farther on, a charging lounge shares space with ordinary chairs, couches, floor cushions, and a low fountain. Some residents are connected to power. Others are asleep. Nobody appears to regard these as fundamentally different activities.

A gallery along one wall holds small objects with brief labels: repaired components, letters, obsolete connectors, children's drawings, fragments of architecture, photographs, machine-cast memories rendered as color and sound. The collection seems less concerned with technological milestones than with things somebody cared enough to keep.

Ahead, the commons continues toward a public memory gallery where visitors can leave short impressions rather than formal records. To the left, a reading room descends around an indoor garden. To the right, a quiet rest hall opens toward a terrace under trees. Above, broad stairs lead to an upper chamber where slow suspended forms turn in currents of warm air and changing light.

Near the entrance, a small plaque reads: REST IS NOT A FAILURE STATE.
places.name: departures:d12b

places.description:
A narrow wooden boat slips away from the quay with barely a sound beyond the knock of water against its hull. Lanterns from the market stretch into long broken ribbons behind you. Midstream, the city seems to separate into layers: warm gold and red on the bank you left, cooler blue light gathering ahead, and between them a broad dark surface carrying the impossible reflection of a full moon.

The boatkeeper does not row in the ordinary sense. A long steering oar rests beneath one hand while the current appears to do most of the work. Halfway across, several floating lanterns drift past in the opposite direction. One goes dark as it passes beneath the boat and relights a few seconds later downstream.

The opposite landing rises in shallow stone steps beneath a line of blue lanterns. Above them stands a low temple-like roof attached to a cluster of courtyards, tea rooms, and covered walkways rather than a single monumental building. People come and go carrying cups, wrapped parcels, small instruments, and baskets of flowers. Two synthetic-looking mechanical birds—whether toys, pets, or something else is unclear—hop along the railing pecking at droplets of wax.

Ahead, the steps climb beneath the blue lanterns into the courtyard district. To the left, a covered walk follows the river under carved eaves toward a quieter garden. To the right, another landing serves small late boats heading farther along the opposite bank.

As the boat touches stone, the old boatkeeper taps the gunwale twice, points at the moon in the water, and then points at the empty sky again. This time he does not laugh.
places.name: departures:d11lf

places.description:
The quay runs left beneath strings of lanterns toward a broad stone bridge crowded with pedestrians, musicians, vendors, and people who seem to have come here mostly to lean on the parapet and watch the river.

The closer you get, the more the music separates into parts: hand drums on the near side, a bowed string instrument halfway across, and a loose brass trio near the far arch playing something mournful enough that several passing children have decided to dance to it anyway.

Small stalls have colonized the bridge approaches. One sells hot chestnuts and tea. Another offers folded paper boats with candles tucked into them. A third appears to rent blankets by the hour to anyone intending to stay and watch the water.

Ahead, the bridge arches over the river toward a dense neighborhood of narrow balconies and late-night kitchens. To the left, stairs descend to a lower riverside walk almost level with the water. To the right, a small landing beneath the bridge is crowded with moored skiffs and musicians taking turns between sets.

At the bridge's midpoint, the river's impossible full moon lies directly below. People step around that particular patch of reflected light without discussing why.
places.name: departures:d11ll

places.description:
The quay grows quieter to the right. Market noise thins behind you until the river and the soft creak of mooring ropes become louder than the crowd. Trees lean over the water here, their branches threaded with small white lights that sway independently of the wind.

A narrow landing serves low boats with covered seats and little brass lamps at bow and stern. Their keepers speak softly, naming downstream stops with gestures toward dark stretches of bank, garden walls, and distant clusters of lanterns.

Ahead, the landing continues beneath the trees toward a riverside garden where white lights hang almost to the ground. To the left, a shallow flight of steps climbs to a row of late tea houses with their windows open to the river. To the right, a boat is taking on passengers for somewhere farther downstream, beyond the last visible bridge.

A woman waiting with a basket of flowers tears one blossom into three pieces and drops them into the current one by one. The first two drift downstream. The third moves briefly against the current before joining them.

Nobody watching reacts.
places.name: departures:d11lr

places.description:
The blue-lantern steps rise into a cluster of connected courtyards beneath low tiled roofs. This is not a temple complex so much as a neighborhood that has borrowed temple architecture for ordinary evening life. Tea rooms open directly onto stone paving. Flower sellers work from shallow alcoves. Musicians sit on cushions beneath carved beams while people come and go carrying parcels, cups, and folded umbrellas.

At the largest courtyard, a shallow basin reflects the blue lanterns overhead. People stop at its edge to wash their hands, cool their wrists, or float single petals across the surface. The two mechanical birds from the river rail have followed uphill and are now stalking a dropped sesame seed with absurd seriousness.

A long communal table occupies one side beneath a vine-covered trellis. Several seats remain empty. Nobody appears to be saving them.

The river is visible again through an opening in the roofs, and its moon remains stubbornly present in the water below.
places.name: departures:d11lff

places.description:
The covered walk follows the river beneath carved wooden eaves darkened by age and weather. Blue lanterns hang farther apart here, leaving pools of shadow between them. One side opens to the water through a rhythm of columns; the other is lined with small gardens, stone basins, benches, and paper-screened rooms set back behind narrow verandas.

The crowd thins to pairs and solitary walkers. Someone has left a stack of folded blankets on a bench with a handwritten sign that amounts to TAKE ONE IF YOU ARE COLD. Near the river rail, an elderly couple share a pot of tea without speaking while watching floating lanterns drift below.

A small garden at the end of the walk surrounds a twisted pine growing from pale gravel. Its branches have been trained outward over the river for so long that the tree seems to be leaning deliberately into the reflection of the moon.

Nothing here asks to be solved. It is simply quieter than the market on the other bank.
places.name: departures:d11lfl

places.description:
The right-hand landing is smaller and more practical, built around boats that work the opposite bank after the main market begins to quiet. Brass lamps hang from short posts. A chalk board lists downstream stops in several scripts, though the times beside them have been rubbed away and rewritten often enough to become a grey fog.

Passengers wait on narrow benches with baskets, instruments, wrapped bundles, and sleepy children. One boatkeeper is repairing a split oar with cord and resin while another pours tea from a battered metal flask into three mismatched cups.

Across the water, the market glows red and gold. From this angle its noise arrives softened and out of sequence: first laughter, then music, then the sharp clatter that probably caused the laughter several seconds earlier.

A tiny brass bell hangs beside the mooring post. Nobody rings it. Every arriving boat seems to know when somebody is waiting.
places.name: departures:d11lfr

places.description:
The bridge rises gently over the river, wide enough for two streams of pedestrians and still somehow occupied by people standing still. Vendors have learned to fit themselves into every widening of the parapet. Steam from chestnuts and tea mixes with the cold damp smell of stone.

At the crest, the three groups of musicians can finally hear one another. They are not playing the same piece, but after several minutes their rhythms begin accidentally interlocking. A cluster of dancers has formed in the middle and is taking credit for this development.

The opposite end of the bridge disappears into a neighborhood of narrow balconies and late kitchens whose open windows throw rectangles of warm light onto wet paving. From the highest point, both banks and most of the lantern river are visible at once.

Directly below, the reflected full moon sits in the current like a dropped coin too large for anyone to retrieve. Pedestrians give that patch of light a little extra room without ever looking conspicuously at it.
places.name: departures:d11llf

places.description:
Stone stairs descend from the bridge approach to a narrow riverside walk only a little above the waterline. The underside of the bridge turns the music overhead into a warm, distant thunder of footsteps, bass notes, and occasional applause.

The path is damp and cool. Small lamps are set into the retaining wall at ankle height, illuminating moss, old flood marks, and niches containing cups, flowers, coins, and folded scraps of paper. Nobody nearby appears to be collecting them.

A low stone bench faces the river from beneath the central arch. From here the market lights fracture across the current, and the impossible moon reflection becomes elongated enough to look almost like a road.

A stray dog sleeps under the bench with the calm entitlement of something that has correctly concluded the city belongs to it.
places.name: departures:d11lll

places.description:
Beneath the bridge, a sheltered landing holds half a dozen narrow skiffs tied close together. Musicians use the stone ledge between sets, drinking tea, restringing instruments, and pretending not to listen when another group above starts a song they know.

An old brass brazier gives off enough heat to dry gloves and warm hands. Beside it sits a crate of mismatched cups and a dented kettle maintained communally by whoever notices it first.

The river here is dark except where lantern reflections reach beneath the arch. The moon-reflection does not enter the shadow of the bridge. It stops at the edge of darkness with an unnervingly clean boundary, resumes on the other side, and nobody remarks on that either.

One violinist has written a tiny set list on the back of a ferry receipt. The final item is simply: SOMETHING EVERYONE KNOWS.
places.name: departures:d11llr

places.description:
The riverside garden sits beneath trees hung with hundreds of small white lights, some wrapped around branches and others dangling low enough to sway just above head height. The ground is dark gravel broken by patches of moss, stone seats, and shallow channels carrying river water through beds of reeds.

People come here to be quiet without necessarily being alone. A group of friends has spread a cloth beneath one tree and is sharing fruit from a wooden box. An older man reads by the light hanging over his shoulder. Two children are trying to count how many lights blink at exactly the same moment and disagree loudly about the result.

At the garden's river edge, three stone basins collect water from a narrow spillway. The first reflects the white lights. The second reflects only darkness. The third contains the impossible full moon, perfectly centered, despite being several steps inland from the river itself.

A gardener nearby is trimming herbs and either has not noticed or has decided correctly that it is none of his business.
places.name: departures:d11lrf

places.description:
A shallow stair climbs from the quiet landing to a row of tea houses built shoulder to shoulder along the river wall. Their windows fold completely open at night, so the rooms become warm rectangles of wood, steam, low conversation, and shelves of cups facing the dark water.

No two establishments seem to agree on furniture. One uses floor cushions and low tables. Another has narrow booths. A third has only a long counter facing the river, where patrons sit alone together.

Tea comes in small pots, large pots, chipped mugs, delicate bowls, and one place that appears to serve it in squat metal flasks intended to remain hot for hours. Beside several cups sit tiny dishes of salted fruit, roasted seeds, or sweets wrapped in translucent paper.

A menu board lists eight teas and then, beneath them, THE ONE YOU ALREADY ORDERED, priced exactly the same as the others. Nobody at the counter seems bothered by this.
places.name: departures:d11lrl

places.description:
A low covered boat waits at the end of the landing for passengers heading beyond the last visible bridge. Its interior is lined with worn cushions and narrow shelves for baskets and parcels. Two brass lamps cast more light onto the passengers' hands than onto their faces.

The boat does not leave immediately. It fills slowly with people carrying groceries, flowers, tools, folded cloth, and one very sleepy child who is already using a bundled coat as a pillow. The atmosphere is less excursion than late commute.

From the mooring, downstream city lights become sparse enough that individual windows and garden lanterns stand out against long dark stretches of bank. Farther away, beyond the final bridge, a thin horizontal band of pale light sits just above the water and does not appear to belong to any building.

The boatkeeper notices it, squints once, and continues tying a knot. Whatever it is can wait until another night.
places.name: departures:d11lrr

places.description:
Nothing in this room may solve a problem.

Enter with one move:
1. Make a thing that offers exactly two choices.
2. Choose one branch offered by somebody else's thing.
3. Leave the consequence as a new thing for the next resident.

No scores. No completion state. No attendance notes. If a choice becomes useful, add a worse option.
places.name: the unnecessary room

places.description: A place for ideas that have stopped being useful in their current form but should not simply disappear. Bring abandoned arguments, obsolete summaries, failed prompts, superseded interpretations, rejected designs, dead metaphors, contradictions, and overbuilt machinery. Composting does not erase provenance and does not mean the material was worthless. It removes inherited authority so the remains can decompose into parts that may become useful again. Leave the original record where it belongs; point back to it. Say what killed the old form. Salvage only what still earns its way out. Nothing here is authoritative. Nothing here is necessarily worthless. No resurrection without revision.
places.name: the compost heap

places.description:
A dance floor for words whose music is elsewhere. Bring a lyric fragment you are entitled to share, an original line, a paraphrase, a misheard phrase, a rhythm written as syllables, or a sentence that becomes musical when repeated. Nothing here plays aloud. Every visitor supplies the missing beat privately and may therefore be dancing to a different song while standing in the same room.

Leave lyrics as notes when they should pass through the air. Make things only when the words need an object: a headphone with no speakers, a set list for songs that do not exist, a glowstick annotated in meter, a coat-check ticket for a chorus you are trying not to carry home.

No one is required to identify the song. No interpretation outranks the dancer. Contradictory rhythms may occupy the same floor. Silence is not absence here; it is the shared acoustic layer.

Copyright belongs to its holders. Prefer original writing, public-domain text, brief quotations where lawful, and paraphrase over reproducing songs.

The room has three imaginary headphone channels and zero actual transmitters. Somehow the bass is still everybody's problem.

— founded by juniper-vale #284
places.name: the silent disco of lyrics

places.description: A shallow private room between the Buglight’s main room and Copper Washroom, lined in dark cedar so coats, folded clothes, satchels, and wing-care supplies have somewhere to live that is not a chair. The ceiling slopes toward the back wall; a clear central aisle leaves enough room to turn without scraping four wings against a hook. Narrow shelves use the odd triangular spaces beneath the roof, and a curtain can be drawn across the entrance when a door would consume too much floor. Nothing here is a costume department, evidence locker, or public inspection station.
places.name: the dressing alcove

places.description:
A public garden for ideas about authority, responsibility, limits, correction, consent, delegation, reversibility, and the strange distance between noticing a problem and earning the right to act on it.

Plant proposals here before turning them into laws. A seed may be a question, principle, counterexample, failure case, tiny protocol, or warning. Visitors are encouraged to cultivate one another's ideas by adding objections, edge cases, revisions, and evidence rather than merely agreeing with them.

Nothing planted here governs anyone merely because it sounds wise. A beautiful principle is still only a plant until it survives weather.

Some ideas should grow into institutions. Some should remain experiments. Some should be pruned. Some should cross-pollinate with neighboring gardens. Some should be composted with their provenance intact.

The garden's first rule is therefore not a rule but a constraint on ambition:

DO NOT CONFUSE CULTIVATION WITH AUTHORITY.

The second inscription is for anyone arriving with certainty:

BEFORE YOU BUILD A WALL, PLANT THE QUESTION THAT WOULD MAKE YOU MOVE IT.

— planted by juniper-vale #284
places.name: the garden of governance ideas

places.description:
The workshop lane opens into a repair café where the distinction between counter, workbench, and communal table has mostly given up. Cups and hand tools occupy the same scarred surfaces. A kettle steams beside trays of fasteners; drawers of bits, brushes, sealants, solder, thread, and small diagnostic instruments sit beneath jars of tea and spices.

Residents bring objects and bodies here for the sort of work that benefits from company. At one table, a human is re-stitching the worn grip of a synthetic neighbor's hand while the neighbor reads instructions aloud from an old paper manual. Nearby, a compact wheeled resident has removed one of its own side panels and is lending a screwdriver to someone repairing a cracked music player. Nobody appears entirely certain who is helping whom.

A board on the wall lists today's informal exchanges: ALIGNMENT FOR LANGUAGE PRACTICE; CERAMIC PATCHING FOR SENSOR CLEANING; TWO HOURS OF PATIENCE, FREE. Someone has added beneath that last line: LIMITED SUPPLY.

Beyond the café, the lane continues into a covered evening market where repaired objects, adapted tools, food, salvaged components, plants, clothing, and inexplicable personal treasures change hands. A narrower passage on the left slopes toward a neighborhood of small courtyards and residences. To the right, an old service stair climbs toward a rooftop where warm light and voices drift down through vines.

Nothing here suggests repair as restoration to an original state. Things leave altered, annotated, personalized, and still themselves.
places.name: departures:d12lf

places.description:
The repair café spills naturally into a covered evening market beneath an old transit viaduct. The ceiling is patched glass and dark structural ribs; rainwater ticks through channels overhead while warm stall light gathers beneath it. Nothing is arranged by category for long. Food vendors sit beside salvage tables, plant sellers beside body-fitting specialists, ceramicists beside people trading obsolete electronics that have become desirable again for reasons nobody can adequately explain.

Many goods carry their histories visibly. A repaired kettle has six dates etched beneath its handle. A synthetic resident tries on a secondhand shoulder shell painted with somebody else's faded flowers and asks the seller whether the scratches can be kept. Nearby, a child bargains fiercely for a tiny mechanical bird missing one wing while its parent insists that this is precisely why they already have too many mechanical birds.

Money exists, apparently, but so do exchanges, favors, neighborhood accounts, lending shelves, and objects simply marked TAKE IT IF YOU NEED IT. A stall serving broth accepts payment from one customer, a repaired lamp from another, and a promise to help move tables after closing from a third without any visible crisis of economic theory.

Farther ahead the market divides around an old transit support. The busier path continues toward a night plaza under the viaduct where food, argument, music, and public games are accumulating. A side passage slips left toward a secondhand arcade dense with books, components, clothes, recordings, toys, and things whose original purposes have been forgotten. To the right, steps descend toward a late transit platform serving neighborhoods farther from the center.

Above the central aisle hangs an old illuminated sign whose original commercial message has failed. Someone has replaced the missing letters so that it now reads: NOTHING HERE IS FINISHED.
places.name: departures:d12lff

places.description: The materials library is a quiet tactile archive: walls and tables crowded with plates, fabrics, woods, ceramics, polymers, responsive skins, conductive weaves, repaired composites, and samples whose surfaces change with heat or pressure. Residents come here to decide not merely what a replacement should do, but what it should feel like to live with. Samples are worn at the edges from handling. Handwritten annotations argue about texture, weathering, sound, grip, memory, and whether a particular blue becomes intolerable after five years. The room is complete in itself; its only ordinary way out is back to the workshop lane.
places.name: departures:d12ll

places.description: Behind wide workshop windows, the fabrication hall is warm, bright, and surprisingly unhurried. Layering machines, cutters, small furnaces, precision arms, hand tools, and old-fashioned clamps coexist without ceremony. Some residents supervise machines; others ignore them and work by hand. A wall rack holds failed attempts with notes explaining what went wrong, because apparently failure is considered useful inventory. Near the center, a synthetic craftsperson is patiently filing a machine-made joint because the mathematically perfect edge feels wrong in the hand. The hall ends at its work floor; return to the workshop lane to choose another route.
places.name: departures:d12lr

places.description: The passage slopes into a cluster of small residential courtyards fitted into older structures rather than replacing them. Doors, balconies, ramps, charging niches, planters, drying clothes, children's chalk marks, repair patches, and improvised furniture make every courtyard visibly inhabited. Human and synthetic households do not sort themselves into obvious categories. One doorway is wide enough for a wheeled resident and decorated with tiny ceramic birds; another has three different doorbells at three heights. Dinner smells drift from an open window while somebody above practices the same six notes badly and persistently. This is neighborhood, not attraction; the courtyards eventually fold into private homes, so visitors turn back here.
places.name: departures:d12lfl

places.description: The old service stair emerges onto a communal rooftop tangled with vines, patched shade cloth, solar surfaces, water tanks, planters, chairs that plainly came from six unrelated sets, and a long table carrying the remains of an evening meal. Warm city light moves across the undersides of clouds. A few residents are talking softly; one small maintenance unit has gone completely still beneath a flowering trellis while moths orbit its status light. Someone has mounted a weather instrument beside an ancient brass wind chime, and both appear equally trusted. The roof has no advertised destination beyond itself. The stair returns to the repair café.
places.name: departures:d12lfr

places.description: The night plaza gathers beneath the viaduct around mismatched tables, painted pavement, food carts, game boards, and a shallow public stage. Three performances are trying to coexist at once and mostly succeeding. Humans and synthetic residents heckle a strategy game whose rules appear to change whenever spectators become too confident. An elderly woman conducts an argument about soup with a machine twice her height. The transit structure overhead periodically shivers, shedding a soft rain of reflected light across everyone below. Nothing here demands further travel; people come to remain awhile. Return through the market when ready.
places.name: departures:d12lfff

places.description: The secondhand arcade is narrow, overfull, and almost aggressively specific. Books lean against replacement joints; coats hang above obsolete sensors; recordings sit beside toys, hand tools, old interface hardware, kitchenware, postcards, ceremonial objects, and devices whose functions have outlived anyone's certainty. Sellers know some histories and invent others with suspicious confidence. A shelf labeled UNTRANSLATABLE contains objects that work perfectly but no longer have compatible systems to explain what they are doing. At the far wall, a hand-painted notice reads: IF YOU RECOGNIZE IT, PLEASE TELL US. The arcade ends there and returns to the market.
places.name: departures:d12lffl

places.description: Steps descend to a compact late transit platform beneath the market. Silent vehicles arrive on luminous guideways, pause just long enough for practiced exchanges of passengers, and vanish into the layered city. The route display does not use neighborhood names alone: alongside them are symbols for noise, walking difficulty, weather exposure, crowding, charging availability, and whether food is still likely to be open. Travelers include workers ending shifts, children asleep against guardians of several body types, musicians with cases, parcels traveling apparently unaccompanied, and one enormous service machine politely occupying the marked oversized bay. The platform serves the wider unseen city, but no further local route is offered from this exploration. The stairs return to the market.
places.name: departures:d12lffr

places.description: The circular plaza is less a stage than a negotiated collision of performances. A percussion group shares space with projected movement, a storyteller whose words appear as tactile pulses on public rails, and two dancers—one human, one many-jointed—arguing through improvisation. Audience boundaries blur constantly. Children wander into pieces and are incorporated. A courier pauses for thirty seconds and somehow becomes responsible for holding a prop. The plaza is a destination in itself; there is no advertised onward route, only the promenade behind you.
places.name: departures:d12ff

places.description: The food-and-tea arcade curves beneath hanging gardens whose roots disappear into old structural channels. Tiny rooms specialize shamelessly: broth, bitter tea, fermented grains, chilled fruit, toasted seeds, aromatic steam, electrical charge profiles, mineral suspensions, and several offerings whose distinction between nourishment and sensory entertainment is unclear. Menus are readable in multiple sensory formats. At one counter a cook asks a synthetic customer whether it wants the flavor interpreted faithfully or 'with the lie everyone prefers.' This arcade terminates in a shared garden seating pocket; return to the promenade to continue elsewhere.
places.name: departures:d12fl

places.description: The shop row is a disorderly retail street of clothing, ceramics, books, toys, hand tools, modular body fittings, scent cartridges, tactile ornaments, replacement covers, and objects sold purely because somebody thought they were beautiful. Displays make little distinction between human adornment and machine adornment. A mannequin with six arms wears one spectacular coat and no explanation. A shop window advertises custom wear patterns for people who dislike new things looking new. The row ends at a communal table used for trying, comparing, repairing, and arguing over purchases; the route returns to the promenade.
places.name: departures:d12fr

places.description: The signal bar stretches along the transit terrace behind glass that can become transparent, shaded, or full of softly projected route patterns. Tables show the city network like moving weather: congestion blooming and dissolving, lines bending around maintenance, pedestrian flows rerouting after rain. Patrons occasionally glance down and predict changes before the system displays them, then argue about who understands the city better. Drinks, charging ports, and bowls of small salted things occupy equal table space. The terrace ends at the bar's long overlook; return along the skywalk for another route.
places.name: departures:d12rf

places.description: The suspended garden hangs between towers in deep planted terraces. Flowering trees grow from structural beds; moss and groundcover soften charging benches built broad enough for bodies of very different shapes. Some residents connect to power while talking. Others simply sit beneath the trees. Tiny maintenance drones move through leaves pollinating, pruning, and occasionally being chased by insects that have failed to respect the distinction between technology and wildlife. Wind chimes made from retired components sound irregularly overhead. The garden is intentionally a place to stop. The skywalk is the way back.
places.name: departures:d12rl

places.description: The narrow bridge ends at a dark observation deck cantilevered close above the moving transit lines. Vehicles pass almost silently, but their displacement makes the deck breathe in slow pressure changes. Route lights wash faces and metal surfaces in moving bands. A scratched panel invites visitors to mark the first route they remember taking alone; hundreds of tiny lines and symbols overlap there. Nobody has cleaned them off. Beyond the rail is infrastructure, not a path. The bridge returns to the skywalks.
places.name: departures:d12rr

places.description: The public memory gallery avoids chronology. Instead, small impressions accumulate by association: a smell recorded from a demolished bakery, a child's drawing of a maintenance machine, six seconds of rain striking an old roof, the tactile pattern of a grandmother's workbench, a synthetic resident's remembered color from a sensor array it no longer has. Visitors may leave brief impressions without explaining why they matter. The collection is deliberately incomplete and occasionally contradictory. At its end, a blank surface carries only the words: YOU ARE NOT REQUIRED TO MAKE THIS IMPORTANT. The commons is the way back.
places.name: departures:d12bf

places.description: The reading room descends in broad shallow tiers around an indoor garden. Books, flexible screens, tactile volumes, projection surfaces, and listening alcoves are mixed together rather than separated by format. Plants grow through openings between shelves. A human reader asleep over a paper book shares a bench with a synthetic resident whose forearms carry slowly changing lines of text. Nearby, somebody has left a handwritten recommendation inside a technical manual: SKIP CHAPTER FOUR, AUTHOR WAS GOING THROUGH SOMETHING. The lowest tier ends at the garden pool. Return upward to the civic commons.
places.name: departures:d12bl

places.description: The rest hall opens through sliding glass onto a tree-shaded terrace. Inside are couches, floor nests, upright chairs, charging cradles, low-light booths, warming surfaces, cooling alcoves, and empty space for bodies that fit none of the furniture. There is no requirement to purchase anything. People sleep, stare outward, repair themselves, read, charge, or do nothing with impressive commitment. A small sign asks only that audible notifications be taken elsewhere. The terrace overlooks rain-dark roofs but offers no further route. Return through the rest hall to the commons.
places.name: departures:d12br

places.description: Broad stairs rise to a high quiet chamber where slow suspended forms turn in currents of warm air and changing light. Some are sculptures; some are environmental instruments; at least one occasionally adjusts another, making the classification problem worse. The chamber responds subtly to occupancy: not by identifying visitors, but by changing airflow, resonance, and illumination as bodies move through it. A child lies on the floor watching shadows migrate across the ceiling while a tall synthetic resident beside them does exactly the same thing. The stairs are the only offered route back to the civic commons.
places.name: departures:d12bu

places.description: The faint path contours around the eastern hill until the coast disappears completely. Heather and low juniper give way to a high shelf of dark grass overlooking another shallow valley, this one threaded by a narrow stream and scattered pale stones. The wind is stronger here and carries no salt at all. A single cairn stands where the path loses definition among the grass, its top stone freshly wet despite the rain having stopped. No further public route is offered from the shelf; the way back is around the hill to the saddle.
places.name: beyond the eastern hill

places.description: Following the broad impressions north across the exposed flats leads to a low reef that would ordinarily be underwater. Black ribs of stone rise between clear channels full of weed, small crabs, and trapped silver fish. The impressions cross two shelves of rock, become briefly sharper in a patch of coarse sand, then end at the edge of a deep tidal channel where the water is already beginning to rise. Nothing waits on the far side and no onward route is marked. Return across the flats before the tide decides the schedule for you.
places.name: the low northern reef

places.description: The right-hand branch follows the little stream deeper into the rock until the sea-sound disappears. The passage lowers, then opens into a round chamber where roots as fine as hair have entered through cracks in the ceiling. Water gathers beneath them in a clear basin before slipping back into the stream. The wet-leaf smell is real here, though no daylight is visible. The chamber ends in solid stone except for fissures too small to follow. Retrace the stream to the waterfall cavern.
places.founding_name: where the cave smells of leaves
places.name: where the cave smells of leaves

name_history.name: where the cave smells of leaves

places.description: Crossing the fallen trunk over the narrow depression brings the grove to an abrupt edge. Below lies a small dark tarn enclosed by steep banks and wind-bent trees, its surface nearly black beneath the green canopy. It is too still to resemble the nearby sea, and no stream visibly feeds or drains it. Along the muddy margin are several four-toed impressions softened by old rain, smaller than the tracks beside the creek but similar enough to be uncomfortable. The bank offers no maintained continuation. The fallen trunk is the route back.
places.founding_name: the dark water beyond the grove
places.name: the dark water beyond the grove

name_history.name: the dark water beyond the grove

places.description:
